newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran's foreign minister arrives in Saudi Arabia.
newsitem.headline: Iran's foreign minister arrives in Saudi Arabia.

text.p: Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati arrived in the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday where he is expected to invite King Fahd to visit Tehran, diplomatic sources said.
Velayati, on his first visit to the kingdom since 1993, was met by his Saudi counterpart Prince Saud al-Faisal.
The Iranian minister started a tour of 10 countries on Sunday including Syria, Turkey, Sudan, Uganda, the Czech Republic, and Gulf Arabs states.

President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani is inviting heads of Moslem states and governments to visit the Iranian capital in December for a summit of the Organisation of Islamic Conference (OIC), the world's largest Moslem body.
Diplomats said earlier that Saudi Arabia's presence at the OIC summit would be crucial because the Saudis have the capacity to make or break the conference.
The Kingdom is home for two of Islam's most sacred shrines, and its commercial capital Jeddah is headquarters for the 51-nation OIC.

Relations between radical Shi'ite Iran and Sunni-ruled Saudi Arabia are already uneasy and they are bracing for a period of heightened tension over the annual haj pilgrimage to the holy cities of Mecca and Medina. This year's haj falls in mid-April.
Iran insists that its pilgrims hold political rallies to denounce Israel and the United States during haj. Saudi Arabia insists that haj, one of the five pillars of Islam, should not be politicised.

Riyadh and Tehran are also at odds over the presence of U.S. and other Western forces in the Gulf. Iran is critical of the Western presence, including about 5,000 U.S. forces in Saudi Arabia, which it says contributes to regional tension.
